extracted.intended_audience: corporate registrants, legal counsel, and accounting/finance teams preparing SEC filings for business acquisitions and dispositions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on when and how to report acquisitions, dispositions, and related financial information on Form 8-K and in registration/proxy statements under Regulation S‑X and Form 8‑K rules. Covers significance tests, filing deadlines, required content for Items 1.01, 2.01 and 9.01, and special situations (shells, VIEs, parent/subsidiary, related businesses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form 8‑K filing decision criteria for acquisitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a decision tree: Is the registrant a domestic company (or an FPI electing to file as a domestic issuer)? Do the assets acquired constitute a business pursuant to S‑X Rule 11‑01(d)? Is the significance of the business acquisition greater than 20% per S‑X Rule 1‑02(w) tests? Are audited financial statements required by Item 9.01 currently available? If assets do not constitute a business, check the 10% asset tests in Item 2.01.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the acquisition is a business and >20% significant, Form 8‑K is required (Item 2.01 and Item 9.01). If not a business but assets exceed 10% of consolidated assets, file under Item 2.01. If Item 9.01 information is not yet available, registrant may file Item 2.01 and estimate timing for Item 9.01 (see 4-business-day and 71-day timing rules). Consult advisers if timing/availability problems arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial Form 8‑K filing deadline for significant business acquisitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The initial Form 8‑K reporting consummation of a significant business acquisition must be filed on or before the fourth business day following consummation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The initial Form 8‑K must include, at minimum, the Item 2.01 information (see separate criterion). If financial statements are unavailable, file Item 2.01 by day 4 and provide Item 9.01 information via amendment within the 71-calendar-day extension if eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amended Form 8‑K (Item 9.01) timing and 71‑day extension
rubrics_metrics.description: Amended Form 8‑K containing required audited financial statements and pro forma information must be filed no later than 71 calendar days after the original Form 8‑K due date (i.e., the initial four-business-day deadline).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shell companies (e.g., SPACs) cannot use the 71‑day extension and must provide Item 9.01 information in the initial Form 8‑K. The total available period is typically 4 business days + 71 calendar days (about 75–77 calendar days depending on weekends/holidays). If Item 9.01 information will not be available, consult counsel and consider requesting SEC no-action relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum Item 2.01 content for initial Form 8‑K
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 2.01 initial Form 8‑K must include: the date the transaction was completed; a brief description of what was acquired; the counterparty and any material relationships (including directors/officers); the nature and amount of consideration; additional info if material relationships exist between counterparties and sources of funds; and additional information if the registrant was a shell company immediately before the transaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the minimum disclosures; include any other material information necessary to make the disclosure not misleading. Use Item 8.01 for voluntary additional disclosures if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 9.01 required financial information for acquisitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 9.01 requires audited annual and unaudited interim financial statements of the acquired business (Rule 3‑05 financial statements) and the registrant’s pro forma financial information reflecting the acquisition (S‑X Article 11 pro forma information).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number of periods required depends on significance (see S‑X Rule 3‑05 thresholds). If not available at initial filing, provide via amended Form 8‑K within the 71‑day extension (unless subject to the shell-company exception).

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance tests for acquisitions of businesses (S‑X/Reg S‑X thresholds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance for acquired businesses is determined under S‑X Rule 1‑02(w) tests (revenue, income/loss from continuing operations, total assets) with thresholds that trigger different requirements (e.g., >20% triggers Form 8‑K disclosures; higher thresholds affect number of financial statement periods).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If none of the conditions exceeds 20% no acquired-business financial statements are required for registration; >20% but ≤40% requires at least most recent fiscal year and most recent interim; >40% requires at least two most recent fiscal years and interims. Aggregate impacts exceeding 50% trigger additional disclosure and pro forma requirements (see S‑X Rule 3‑05(b)(2)(iv)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation of related businesses for significance determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Related businesses are combined and treated as a single acquisition for determining significance for Form 8‑K and S‑X purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acquisitions of ‘related’ businesses that, in the aggregate, exceed 20% significance require Form 8‑K reporting. The handbook references related businesses, related real estate operations, and related funds (see specific CFR sections cited).

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance tests and reporting for asset acquisitions that are not businesses (10% tests)
rubrics_metrics.description: When assets acquired do not meet the definition of a business, significance for Item 2.01 is determined under Item 2.01 instructions: the acquisition is significant if the registrant’s share in the net book value (cost) of the assets acquired or disposed exceeds 10% of consolidated total assets, or the amount paid/received for the assets exceeds 10% of consolidated total assets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such asset acquisitions are significant at the 10% level, Item 2.01 disclosures must be made within four business days, and pro forma information must be included if material. The 71‑day extension for Item 9.01 financial statements does not apply to asset acquisitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form 8‑K requirements for significant business dispositions
rubrics_metrics.description: Disposition of a significant business is reported under Item 2.01. Pro forma financial information reflecting the disposition is included under Item 9.01 if applicable; historical financial statements of the disposed business are not required in Form 8‑K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pro forma financial information for dispositions must be filed on a Form 8‑K within four business days of the disposition. The 71‑day extension available for acquired-business financial statements does not apply to dispositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 1.01 (Entry into a Material Definitive Agreement) required disclosures pre‑consummation
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 1.01 requires a brief description of material terms and conditions of the agreement that are material to the registrant. The SEC staff generally expects disclosure of: nature and amount of consideration (or method/exchange ratio/formula); any committed financing arrangements or need for financing to close and material terms; material terms regarding securities ownership or management structure of the combined/surviving company after closing; material conditions to closing; and anticipated timeframes for filing Securities Act registration statements, proxies/information statements, tender offer materials, and closing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include any other material information necessary to avoid being misleading. If a material term is undetermined, affirmatively state so. If registrant is the acquirer, briefly describe the target’s business (operations/revenues) and any information the target disclosed when announcing the transaction. File the agreement as an exhibit in proper EDGAR format within four business days where practicable; redaction of sensitive terms is permitted without confidential treatment request. If unable to prepare EDGAR-formatted exhibit, explain in the Form 8‑K.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parent‑subsidiary transaction reporting rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally, Form 8‑K is not required for transactions between a parent and any wholly owned subsidiary or between two or more wholly owned subsidiaries of a parent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: if a wholly owned subsidiary that is itself a reporting company acquires a significant amount of assets from its parent, the subsidiary (which has the reporting obligation) is required to file a Form 8‑K because the instruction exemption is applied with reference to the company obligated to file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variable interest entity (VIE) consolidation reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Acquisition through consolidation that results in consolidation of a VIE is within the scope of Form 8‑K reporting for significant acquisitions. If the VIE meets the definition of a business and is significant, Item 9.01 (S‑X Rule 3‑05 financial statements and S‑X Rule 11‑01 pro forma) applies. If the VIE is not a business, report under Item 2.01 if significant under that Item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consolidation of a VIE solely due to adoption/amendment of an accounting standard under Subtopic 810‑10 does not trigger a Form 8‑K. For detailed guidance on VIE existence/consolidation, consult consolidation guidance (e.g., KPMG Handbook Consolidation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration/proxy statement timing and 75‑day/74‑day grace period rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether pre‑acquisition financial statements and pro forma information are required in a registration statement depends on whether the acquisition was consummated, whether it was consummated 75 or more days before effectiveness (the '75‑day grace period'), and the effective date or mailing date of the registration/proxy statement. Drafts are evaluated at submission date and staff may not review statements lacking required financials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an acquisition was consummated 75+ days before effectiveness, the tableed significance thresholds determine whether financial statements and pro forma are required at effectiveness. Special rules permit omissions in some narrow circumstances (e.g., registration statements not subject to §230.419 or specific timing conditions). A registrant omitting required acquired-business financials from initial registration must file them on Form 8‑K no later than 75 days after consummation. Certain offerings may proceed before acquired-business financial statements are filed (employee benefit plans, dividend/interest reinvestment plans, securities issued upon conversion/exercise).

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary use of Form 8‑K (Item 8.01) for aggregate significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants may voluntarily use Item 8.01 of Form 8‑K to file information (including historical financial statements and pro forma financial information) for individually insignificant acquisitions when the registrant considers the information important to investors—e.g., where several acquisitions together are or will be significant in the aggregate (such as approaching or exceeding 50% significance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voluntary filing choice is at registrant’s discretion and may be used to permit incorporation by reference into future registration statements or shelf registrations to meet Article 11 requirements.
